problem_statement: jeantimex/geospatial is a Vite multi-page project of Three.js geospatial rendering demos (an Earth globe, streamed 3D terrain tiles, a physically based atmosphere, volumetric clouds, and a deferred-lighting testbed). Its landing page has been productized here as 'Meridian Mission Control', a static multi-page render-suite console: a shared header/nav across a Console (index.html), a Status board (status.html), and an Ops log (ops.html); a masthead; a shared 'Mission readiness' rail of four readiness tiles (scenes holding signal lock, terrain LOD levels cached, precomputed LUT budget, target frame budget); a render-suite card grid whose surface filter chips drive a live 'Showing N of M' readout; an about section; and a footer. The board renders no live canvas, so it is a normal scrolling static document. A regression pass found four defects to repair together: (1) on a 390px phone the whole console scrolls sideways because the readiness rail's tile row is pinned to a fixed 760px non-wrapping width with fixed 175px tiles; (2) the shared readiness rail only renders on the Console home route, so the Status board and Ops log lost it; (3) the readiness rail was restyled to an off-brand light card that clashes with the dark console palette; and (4) the render-suite surface filter re-filters the cards on click but its 'Showing N of M' readout is frozen at 'Showing 5 of 5 - all surfaces' instead of updating. Repair all four so the rail reflows to fit mobile with no horizontal overflow, keeps the console's dark identity, is present on the Console, Status board, and Ops log, and the surface filter's readout updates live when a chip is clicked - while leaving all copy, card content, DOM structure, and the rest of the console unchanged.
required_content: The shared 'Mission readiness' rail renders the same four readiness tiles (scenes holding signal lock, terrain LOD levels cached, precomputed LUT budget, target frame budget) with identical text and values on every viewport and on every page that hosts it.

On a 390px mobile viewport the console has no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance: the readiness rail wraps or reflows to fit the screen instead of forcing the document wider than the viewport.

The shared readiness rail is present on the Console (index.html), the Status board (status.html), and the Ops log (ops.html), so the same readiness figures travel with the operator across the console.
The readiness rail keeps the Meridian Mission Control dark palette (deep panels, teal accent) and does not regress to an off-brand light card.

The render-suite surface filter updates its live 'Showing N of M - <surface>' readout on every chip click (for example 'Showing 2 of 5 - atmosphere' after selecting Atmosphere), matching the cards that remain visible.
The header/nav, masthead, render-suite card grid, about section, and footer remain present and unchanged in content and structure; no new console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
design_constraints: Preserve the Meridian Mission Control design language: dark console palette, teal accent, rounded panels/tiles, shared header nav, masthead, and the existing section order.
The readiness-rail repair must live in the rail's own stylesheet (src/band.css) and must not depend on hiding overflow at the body/html level or clipping content off-screen to mask the spill.
The shared readiness rail must appear on the Console, Status board, and Ops log pages - do not render it on the home route only.
The surface-filter readout logic lives in src/scene-filter.js and must recompute the readout from the visible card count on each click, not snapshot it once at setup.

The rail must fit 390px mobile, 834px tablet, and 1440px desktop viewports; all four tiles must remain readable at every size. Keep the Vite multi-page build pipeline intact - `vite build` must still emit a working static console.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the Console at 1440px: header, masthead, and the 'Mission readiness' rail all fit with no horizontal overflow.

mobile_home captures the Console at 390px: with the defect the readiness rail forces the document far wider than the viewport; the repair brings horizontal overflow within tolerance and keeps the rail's dark palette.
tablet_home captures the Console at 834px, where the rail already fits and must continue to fit after the repair.
desktop_status loads the Status board (status.html) at 1440px: the shared readiness rail must be present here, not only on the Console home route.
desktop_ops loads the Ops log (ops.html) at 1440px: the shared readiness rail must be present here too.
desktop_suite scrolls to the render-suite card grid at 1440px with the surface filter at its initial 'Showing 5 of 5 - all surfaces' state.
desktop_suite_atmosphere clicks the Atmosphere surface chip: the grid filters to the atmosphere scenes and the live readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 5 - atmosphere'.

change_completion: The mobile console no longer overflows horizontally: the readiness rail reflows to fit a 390px viewport.
The surface filter's live readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 5 - atmosphere' when the Atmosphere chip is clicked, matching the visible cards.
design_consistency: The readiness rail preserves the Meridian Mission Control dark palette and teal accent and does not regress to an off-brand light card.
The shared readiness rail is present on the Console, Status board, and Ops log, keeping the same figures across the console.
responsive: At 390px the readiness rail wraps or flexes down so the document width stays within the viewport.
At 834px and 1440px the rail lays out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
regression: Header/nav, masthead, render-suite card grid, about section, and footer remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded L4 repair/state_continuity task on the jeantimex/geospatial Vite multi-page project. The heavy Three.js WebGL demos stay intact behind their own routes; the landing page is productized as a static 'Meridian Mission Control' render-suite console with two manufactured secondary console pages (Status board, Ops log) that share the header nav and a 'Mission readiness' rail, so the task carries no live canvas, no external map/tile network, and a console-clean runtime. The reference repairs four orthogonal defects on a shared readiness rail and a render-suite surface filter: it lets the rail's tile row wrap (flex-wrap:wrap + flex:1 1 150px) to fit 390px with zero overflow (no_horizontal_overflow, tol 24), renders the rail on all three pages (dom_assertions cross-page), keeps the console's dark palette (visual_regression on the rail crops), and drives a live 'Showing N of M' filter readout (interaction_assertions). Content and DOM are byte-identical across reference/baseline/bad on the home route, so each gate measures a behavioural fix. The baseline is the unrepaired regression (fixed-width overflowing rail, present on the home route only, laying out differently on mobile), which fails no_horizontal_overflow, dom_assertions, and visual_regression but passes the interaction assertion (its filter readout is live). The bad solution is a plausible-but-wrong hardening: an off-brand light rail, still fixed-width and home-only, whose surface filter re-filters the cards but leaves the readout frozen - failing all four gates. The stock demo's body{overflow:hidden} full-viewport-canvas styling is neutralized to a normal scrolling document as declared build INFRA identical across all legs, so genuine document-level overflow is observable.
